message.content: In domestic cats and many other felids, the presence of a mane (the long, shaggy fur around the head and neck) is controlled by a dominant allele. In lions, the same principle applies: the allele that produces a full mane in males is dominant over the allele that results in a short‑haired or absent mane. Thus, if a lion inherits one copy of the mane allele from either parent, it will develop a mane. This is why most male lions have prominent manes while females do not—female lions typically inherit two copies of the recessive allele that does not produce a mane.
